topic: slides-to-video — a Claude Code skill that turns a topic into a narrated, designed video
audience: developers and technical creators evaluating the tool
goal: a punchy product film that shows what it is and why it's different
thesis: slides-to-video turns a topic into a narrated, designed video through an agent pipeline — free by default and gated by deterministic checks, so the output is both creative and trustworthy.
mechanism: A storyboard.json is the single source of truth. An agent pipeline builds it: content-planner decides what each beat teaches, design-director designs how it looks (running a template contest and per-beat color worlds), scriptwriter writes the narration, and a critic panel audits it. Python scripts then render the media: edge-tts synthesizes free neural narration with per-word timings, ffmpeg and PIL burn karaoke captions, and either the HTML slide tier or the Remotion cinematic tier produces the frames.

evidence.claim: Runs free by default — neural TTS (edge-tts), ffmpeg, and PIL captions need no paid API key.
evidence.source_ref: skill: scripts/tts.py, render.py, SKILL.md Tools section

evidence.claim: Karaoke captions highlight the spoken word, timed to real per-word start times.
Deterministic gates run before every render: validate (structure, captions, motion), keyframe_qa (visual QA), rhythm_qa (pacing), check_av (A/V drift).

The cinematic tier moves a camera over 3D depth planes, with a catalogue of bold templates re-skinned from one accent, and native components (terminal, HUD, spotlight, connector, giant type, materialized metaphor).

why_it_matters: Most AI video tools trade control for polish or polish for control. This one keeps a human-editable storyboard, makes the creative choices explicit and auditable, and still runs free — so a developer gets a cinematic result without giving up trust or budget.
the_one_thing: A topic becomes a narrated, designed video — agent-planned, deterministically checked, free by default.
